summary_paragraph: A male patient with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis and known coronary artery disease presented with recurrent chest pain that awoke him from sleep, relieved by nitroglycerin. Evaluation revealed new EKG changes and a positive pharmacologic stress test showing a reversible perfusion defect in the RCA/LCx territory. He underwent cardiac catheterization, which confirmed 90% stenoses in the right coronary artery at the edge of a prior stent and in the mid-distal segment. Rotational atherectomy was performed, followed by placement of two drug-eluting stents. The procedure was successful with no complications. He remained chest pain-free post-procedure, completed a dialysis session, and was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to continue dual antiplatelet therapy and resume his regular hemodialysis schedule.
problems: Atherosclerotic heart disease of native coronary artery with unstable angina pectoris
Hypertensive chronic kidney disease with stage 5 chronic kidney disease or end stage renal disease
Presence of coronary angioplasty implant and graft
Other nonspecific abnormal finding of lung field
Personal history of transient ischemic attack (TIA), and cerebral infarction without residual deficits
